messages.body_plain:
This has been reported as Issue 330 on github: https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/330

On Friday, April 17, 2015 at 1:09:57 AM UTC-7, Wesley Goi wrote:
> ran into the same problem...
> all the paths will be plotted when you remove `key:= ~id` from the ggvis instructions.
>
> Any update on this?
>
> On Tuesday, 24 March 2015 23:19:30 UTC+8, Chris Jackson wrote:
> > I'm trying to draw multiple paths efficiently by grouping the data using group_by.  I also want a "key" variable for future handling of mouse events.  Using ggvis (0.4.1) + shiny (0.11.1) + dplyr (0.4.1).
> >
> > I can't work out why this draws only one of the paths corresponding to the three groups in the data:
> >
> > mtc <- mutate(mtcars, id=factor(1:nrow(mtcars)))
> > runApp(list(
> >     ui = bootstrapPage(
> >         ggvisOutput("ggvis")
> >     ),
> >     server = function(input, output) {
> >         mtc %>% group_by(cyl) %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, key:=~id, stroke = ~factor(cyl)) %>% layer_paths() %>%
> >           bind_shiny("ggvis")
> >     }
> > ))
> >
> > whereas running ggvis directly, bypassing shiny, gets all three paths drawn.
> >
> > mtc %>% group_by(cyl) %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, key:=~id, stroke = ~factor(cyl)) %>% layer_paths()
> >
> > It also works via shiny if the key is removed from the ggvis() call.
> >
> > In the non-working shiny version, it sometimes draws all three paths, and then immediately redraws using only one of them.
> >
> > Chris
> >

messages.subject: Re: ggvis forum
messages.body_plain:
The person who created the package (Hadley Wickham) answers questions here. If you need something more timely, you might try Stack Overflow as it has a much larger user base.

As for an active community, somewhere in the documentation Wickham notes that ggvis is still in development and probably not suitable for production. However, given the popularity of ggplot, it seems a pretty good bet that, longer term, ggvis will have a fairly large user base. Just have to have a little patience while it finishes baking.

messages.subject: interactive histograms with ggvis
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to creative an interactive plot using ggvis for dynamic variables.

For example,
mtcars %>% ggvis(input_select(names(mtcars), map = as.name <http://as.name>),input_select(names(mtcars),map = as.name <http://as.name>))
       %>% layer_points()

While this works, a similar approach to histograms isn't working.

Example:
mtcars %>% ggvis(input_select(names(mtcars), map = as.name <http://as.name>))
       %>% layer_histograms()

results in Error: Visual property x.update is not a variable.

Same thing for density plot as well. Can someone suggest what I'm doing wrong?

messages.subject: How to take the value of Radio button to draw a specific ggvis plot?
messages.subject_clean: How to take the value of Radio button to draw a specific ggvis plot?
messages.body_plain:
I have this shiny app where I am taking inputs from the user and depending on the type of plot the user wants it will show that plot. But I am unable to take the value of the radio button on the app and use it to draw a specific ggvis plot because the "input$ " value can only be used within a render* function which I am not using here because I am drawing with ggvis.

My ui.R file -

library(ggvis)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("Xvar", "Choose X variable", choices = colnames(the.data), selected = colnames(the.data)[[2]] ),
      selectInput("Yvar", "Choose Y variable", choices = colnames(the.data), selected = colnames(the.data)[[3]] ),
      selectInput("IDvar", "Choose ID variable", choices = colnames(the.data), selected = colnames(the.data)[[4]] ),
      uiOutput("choose_COVvar"),
      uiOutput("choose_COVn"),
      br()
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(type = "tabs",
                  tabPanel("Data Exploration",
                           uiOutput("plot_type"),
                           br(),
                           ggvisOutput("ggvis_xy_plot")),
                           ggvisOutput("ggvis_profile_plot")
      )
    )
  )
))
server.R file -
library(ggvis)
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  the.data <<- mtcars

  output$plot_type <- renderUI({
    fluidRow(
      column(4, offset = 1,
             radioButtons("PlotMethod", h5("Plot type"), c("XY Scatter plot",
                                                           "profile plot"))
      )
    )
  })

  flex.data <- reactive({
    x.name <- input$Xvar
    y.name <- input$Yvar
    id.name <- input$IDvar

    x.data <- the.data[, x.name]
    y.data <- the.data[, y.name]
    ID.t <- the.data[, id.name]
    new.data <- data.frame(x.data, y.data, ID.t)
  })

  lb <- linked_brush(keys = 1:nrow(flex.data()), "red")

  flex.data %>%
    ggvis(~x.data, ~y.data) %>%
    layer_points(fill := lb$fill, fill.brush := "red") %>%
    lb$input()  %>%
    layer_points(fill := "red", data = reactive(flex.data()[flex.data()$ID.t %in%
                                                              flex.data()[lb$selected(), ]$ID.t, ])) %>%
    bind_shiny("ggvis_xy_plot")

  flex.data %>%
    ggvis(~x.data, ~y.data) %>%
    layer_points() %>%
    layer_lines() %>%
    bind_shiny("ggvis_profile_plot")
})

As you can see, currently both the scatter plot and the line plot is there but I want it to be just one depending on the radio button above, the user has pressed.

Any help will be greatly appreciated. Thanks
